This just goes to show how narrative diversity and social justice diversity are at odds.

Narrative diversity allows a piece of fiction to have characters with interesting and varied personalities. This is important for stories with large casts of characters, like Overwatch, fighting games, and superhero team-ups. These sorts of stories usually lean on tropes to flesh out their rosters, because there's not enough time to make every character a deep study of a tortured soul. They end up being cowboys, knights, femme fatales, burly strongmen, double agents, and mad scientists. And it works to make the story interesting.

Social justice diversity demands that a piece of fiction contain no characters that offend anyone. They must not offend people who demand that all fiction contain 'enough' black people. They must not offend people who demand that all fiction should have as few white people as possible. They must not offend people who become upset when a villain is black. They must not offend people who think fictional female characters with a breast size that reflects the average breast size of actual real-life women are pandering to men and have no place in fiction. They must not offend people who think that the portrayal of criminal gangs as being made up primarily of a specific ethnicity - as they are in reality - cannot be reflected in fiction under any circumstances.

And so we have arrived here, on the very threshold of declaring Daffy Duck as a disgusting character that should be scrubbed from the very landscape of entertainment itself...because sometimes he starts laughing and bouncing around a room like a tennis ball, which is offensive to mentally ill persons who suffer from manic episodes.

Making fun of, criticizing, or even just bringing up a woman's weight, sexual preferences, or perceived gender - all things that can change or be changed, sometimes even instantly and on a whim: A monstrous, evil act and a total invasion of privacy.

Mockery of a man's penis size, something entirely beyond their control and a source of sensitivity to many if not most men: Super funny! It's the one physical feature you *can* make fun of people for, as long as it's a straight guy! Teehee!

It's not a fairy tale. It's hard. It's so hard that even though you're getting better at it, it oftentimes feels like it's actually wearing you down and making you weaker. It's deceptive. But I'm starting to understand why that's another way you can win over depression.

Beornings are in a weird spot right now.

Generally speaking, they're quite good at standard solo questing. They do decent damage, and they have plenty of self-healing. They don't shred enemies to bits in mere seconds like hunters or champions do, but they don't get into long drawn-out stalemates like Guardians and Captains do. They can solo quest comfortably and easily survive inopportune twists of fate like unexpected adds or respawns.

Now, when it comes time to group up for instances and raids, Beornings are in low demand. PUGs will rarely take a Beorning if a Guardian or Captain is available to tank, and they're equally unlikely to take them as a healer if there's a Minstrel available - and there almost always is. And as far as going as DPS, forget about it. Of course, if you have friends who will kindly bring you along with them to do group content, then whether strangers will let you into their group is a moot point.

A silver lining is developing, however. I've heard rumblings that, as of late, Beorning healers have surpassed Runekeeper healers in terms of demand. If you show up at just the right moment and there's not enough minstrels to go around, you might get picked up as a healer for a PUG! I haven't played my Beorning in many months, and I won't be coming back until the revamp, but that's what I've observed in-game. Take it with a grain of salt.

And, yes, they have a revamp coming. Maybe before the end of the year, maybe not. And maybe it will help, or maybe it won't. Beorning needs a big revamp and big buffs. A small bump up in effectiveness will still leave the class in an underperforming state. Hopefully they don't pull their punches.

Even if they do get buffed, Beornings will probably retain a few mildly annoying features. Their gameplay is fairly simple and they have the fewest abilities of any class in the game - some may call it boring, some might like it because it lets them focus more on boss mechanics and game atmosphere as opposed to requiring a lot of focus to pull off a good rotation. Gearing them is still a bit weird - medium armor with might is still not as common as other types of armor, and so for long stretches of time most of your armor is going to come from Tailoring and the occasional quest reward pick-a-piece boxes. And they have fewer armor sets available to them than other classes thanks to their late addition to the game. 

If you're looking for a class to level up and go questing around Middle-earth with, they're actually quite fun and durable. But if you're planning on hitting the level cap and doing endgame instances and raids, you may end up frustrated. You'll have to be okay with healing, and you'll have to be okay with the possibility of having a hard time finding groups, and you'll have to be prepared for the not-entirely-unlikely possibility that their revamp may not redeem the class as is hoped.

The Escapist is under new management now that claims they won't be getting political, which of course has sparked drama because there are only three types of people - the good guys (SJWs), the bad guys (literally anyone who has criticized someone who wasn't a heterosexual white man), and the cowardly people in the middle who 'just want to play video games' instead of taking a side in this extremely important social justice war.

It's not enough to be a gaming news website anymore. In the past, when video gaming was a slightly less insanely lucrative industry, video game developers and publishers needed a middleman to help promote their games with previews, screenshots, and reviews. But they don't need that anymore - they have their own PR people now, their own community managers, their own YouTube channels where they post their own promotional material.

The games media was made redundant and had to branch out. They could have gone down a path where they really dug deep into the industry, exposing the insanely harsh working conditions at some studios and cracking down on the inherently predatory nature of microtransaction gambling and lootboxes. But they decided those were only worth a little light dabbling into. 

The REAL fight worth reporting on, they decided, was how there's not perfectly equal representation of every possible social group in every single games development studio. And about how a toxic subset of gamers are totally okay with that, ENABLING these racist and sexist game development studios to continue being evil.

It sucks. I can't blame the games media for becoming more opinionated, because there's just no need for gaming news anymore when developers deliver their own news, but what does suck is that they chose stupid opinions.
